title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PERFORMANCE OF CPGRAMS
body_text:
The Ministry/Department wise details of grievances received, disposed of and pending on the CPGRAMS portal during FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26 is enclosed at Annexure-I.
The Comprehensive Guidelines for Effective Redressal of Public Grievances issued on 23rd August 2024 advises the grievance redressal timelines of 21 days. The details of Ministry/Department wise average disposal time in the year 2025-26 are enclosed at Annexure-II .
To independently assess the citizen satisfaction on grievance resolution on CPGRAMS, a Feedback Call Centre is operational since July 2022.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

enrichment.summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, provided Ministry/Department-wise data on grievances received, disposed of and pending on the CPGRAMS portal for FY 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (as on 05-08-2026). The reply also referenced the Comprehensive Guidelines for Effective Redressal of Public Grievances issued on 23 August 2024, which prescribe a 21-day grievance redressal timeline, and noted that a Feedback Call Centre has been operational since July 2022 to independently assess citizen satisfaction with grievance resolution.
enrichment.context:
CPGRAMS (Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) is the online platform administered by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) that allows citizens to lodge grievances against any Central Government Ministry/Department or State, which are then forwarded to the concerned nodal officers for redressal. It is a key instrument of India's governance reform agenda aimed at improving accountability, transparency and citizen-centric administration, and is often cited in discussions on e-governance and the Right to Public Service-type frameworks even though no umbrella central grievance redressal law currently exists in India (attempts like the Citizens' Charter and Grievance Redressal Bill have lapsed in Parliament).

The data show massive volumes—over 1.6-1.7 crore grievances received annually across ministries—with pendency fluctuating year to year (e.g., total pendency fell sharply from about 1.06 lakh at the end of FY2023-24 to about 62,000 at the end of FY2024-25). The 21-day redressal timeline introduced via the August 2024 guidelines reflects DARPG's continuing push to tighten grievance disposal timelines (earlier norms specified 30 days), and the Feedback Call Centre represents an attempt to move beyond mere disposal metrics to actual outcome/satisfaction-based evaluation, addressing past criticism that grievances were being closed without genuine resolution.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements about CPGRAMS (Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System):
1. It is administered by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances.
2. As per the Comprehensive Guidelines issued in August 2024, the prescribed grievance redressal timeline is 21 days.
3. A Feedback Call Centre under CPGRAMS has been operational since July 2022 to assess citizen satisfaction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: All three statements are supported by the release: CPGRAMS is under DARPG, the August 2024 guidelines set a 21-day redressal timeline, and the Feedback Call Centre has been functioning since July 2022.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Comprehensive Guidelines for Effective Redressal of Public Grievances' referred to in a recent Rajya Sabha reply was issued by which body?
options: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)
prelims_questions.explanation: CPGRAMS and its associated grievance redressal guidelines fall under the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of CPGRAMS in strengthening citizen-centric governance in India. What are the persistent challenges in ensuring timely and substantive redressal of public grievances, and how can they be addressed?

Examine the significance of outcome-based feedback mechanisms, such as the CPGRAMS Feedback Call Centre, in evaluating the effectiveness of grievance redressal systems as opposed to mere quantitative disposal metrics.
